topicName: Runner Group Management, Access Control, and Network Isolation
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Enterprise GitHub Actions: Runner Group Management, Access Control, and Network Isolation"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As organizations scale their usage of GitHub Actions, managing compute resources securely becomes critical. By default, GitHub-hosted runners share a public IP pool, and self-hosted runners are scoped to repositories globally unless organized correctly. This tutorial covers how to implement runner groups, restrict access to specific repositories or organizations, and achieve network isolation for secure CI/CD pipelines."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Runner Groups"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Runner groups allow enterprise and organization administrators to logically segment self-hosted runners. Instead of exposing all runners to every repository, you can group them based on security tiers, environment types (e.g., production vs. staging), or dedicated compliance requirements."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Default Group: Every organization has a default runner group where new self-hosted runners are automatically placed if no other group is specified."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Custom Groups: Created via the GitHub API or UI, these allow granular access policies and repository targeting."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Configuring Access Control"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Access control restricts which repositories can dispatch workflows to a specific runner group. This prevents less trusted repositories from executing code on powerful or sensitive self-hosted infrastructure."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Example GitHub CLI command to create a restricted runner group\ngh api --method POST /orgs/YOUR_ORG/actions/runner-groups \\n  -f name='Production-Runners' \\n  -f visibility='selected' \\n  -F selected_repository_ids[]=12345678"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the example above, visibility is set to 'selected', meaning only the specified repository IDs can target runners in the 'Production-Runners' group using runs-on: [self-hosted, Production-Runners]."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Implementing Network Isolation"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Network isolation ensures that your self-hosted runners operate within a secure corporate Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) or on-premise network, shielded from inbound public internet traffic while safely reaching out to GitHub."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Outbound-Only Communication: Self-hosted runners require outbound access (HTTPS port 443) to GitHub endpoints (github.com, *.githubusercontent.com, and api.github.com) but do not need inbound open ports."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Firewall and Proxy Configuration: Route runner traffic through corporate proxy servers or explicit firewall allowlists to secure data exfiltration paths."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Registering a Runner to a Specific Group"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"When deploying self-hosted runners (e.g., via Kubernetes or virtual machine automation scripts), you must assign them to the target runner group during the configuration phase."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"./config.sh --url https://github.com/YOUR_ORG --token YOUR_TOKEN --runnergroup 'Production-Runners' --labels 'secure,linux,x64'"},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Verification and Best Practices"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always verify your security posture by testing unauthorized workflow triggers. A repository not explicitly granted access to a runner group should fail with a routing error when attempting to use those labels."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rotate runner registration tokens frequently to prevent unauthorized host additions."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ephemeral Runners: Use ephemeral runners (passing --once to config.sh) so that each job runs on a fresh, destroyed environment, preventing state pollution and persistence attacks."}]
